newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier drifts lower on plane order.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier drifts lower on plane order.

text.p: Bombardier Inc shares fell on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Tuesday after the company said it won a $1.4 billion contract to supply 50 of its 70-seat passenger jets to AMR Corp's American Eagle airlines.
Bombardier class B shares slipped 0.20 to 29.95. Traders and analysts said the stock price was likely off since the market had expected Bombardier to win all or part of the big order.
"I think it's neutral for the stock price. There has been so much positive price movement in the stock that this is priced in," said Margaret Cornish-Kehoe, analyst at ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
"I think that had it has been in the market...so the stock is drifting," said a trader.

The order for Bombardier's 70-seat jet came as American Eagle split a $2.4 billion plane purchase order between the Montreal-based aerospace and transportation equipment manufacturer and rival Embraer SA, a Brazil state-owned plane maker.
American Eagle told a news conference at the Paris air show on Tuesday that it was also buying 42 of Embraer's 50-seat regional jets and taking options for a further 25 planes.
In Paris, Bombardier Aerospace President Robert Brown made clear to reporters that the sale price offered by Embraer for its 50-seat jet was too low for Bombardier to match.
Analyst Cornish-Kehoe said Bombardier appeared to decide that it would not jeopardize the healthy profit margins in its 50-seat Regional Jet program by trying to match Embraer's low bid.
Bombardier spokesman Colin Fisher said that despite losing the 50-seat jet order to Embraer, Bombardier remained the world leader in the regional jet sector, with a more than 50 percent market share.
"We don't expect to win every contract, just a large majority of them," he said.
Fisher said American Eagle's firm order for 25 of its 70-seat Canadair Regional Jets plus options for 25 more was the largest to date for the plane and the first from a North American customer.
It was also the largest single order for the 70-seat jet, which was officially launched in January.
"It's very significant. It helps an already very good start for the airplane and we see it as a major step in increasing our (regional jet) market share," Fisher said.

Bombardier expects that the 70-seat jet to take flight in the first quarter of 1999, and be certified by the U.S. FAA in the third quarter of 2000, with the first deliveries to customers coming in the third quarter of 2000.
Deliveries of Bombardier's 70-seat jet to American Eagle are scheduled to begin in early 2001.

Bombardier is producing five of its 50-seat Regional Jets each month and has the capacity to increase that rate to seven monthly. No decision on increasing the production rate was pending, Fisher said.
Bombardier expected to produce 60 of its 50-seat Regional Jets this year compared with 56 last year, he said.
